SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
S. I. Special Branch Station,
REPORT
File No. REGISTRY
Date January 10, 1940.

Subject Reported establishment of large Japanese company to collect
scrap iron in China.

Made by D. S. Kamashita Forwarded by D. I. Crawford.

With reference to the attached extract from
the North China Daily News dated January 8, 1940,
regarding the reported establishment of a large
Japanese company to collect scrap iron in China, I
have to state that this newspaper report appears
to have no foundation.

Enquiries have been conducted at various
quarters but so far no information corroborating
the newspaper report that a large Japanese company
was recently formed with the purpose of collecting
scrap iron in China, was obtainable.

Shortly after the withdrawal of the Chinese
forces from districts surrounding Shanghai, the
local Japanese Residents' Corporation employed a
large number of coolies and engaged in the work of
collecting scrap iron in and outside Shanghai at the
request of the Japanese Military authorities. The
scrap iron collected by the Japanese Residents'
Corporation was dumped on a piece of waste ground in
the vicinity of Chemulpo Road Jetty, from where the
material was shipped to Japan. This work was
completed towards the end of 1938, and it is believed
that insufficient scrap iron still remains to warrant
the establishment of a large company to collect it.

C. 10/1
D. Kamashita
D. S.

主题 据报成立大型日本公司以在华收集废铁。

呈报人 D. S. Kamashita 转呈人 D. I. Crawford。

关于随附的1940年1月8日《字林西报》摘录，该报报道据称成立了一家大型日本公司以在华收集废铁，本人须声明，该新闻报道似乎毫无根据。

经向各方查询，但迄今未能获得任何证实该新闻报道的信息，即最近成立了一家旨在华收集废铁的大型日本公司。

在中国军队撤出上海周边地区后不久，当地日本居留民团应日本军方当局的要求，雇佣了大量苦力，在上海内外从事收集废铁的工作。日本居留民团收集的废铁被倾倒在乍浦路码头附近的一块空地上，随后这些材料被运往日本。这项工作于1938年底完成，据信剩余的废铁数量不足，无需为此成立一家大型公司进行收集。

据一份中文报告称，日本人已组织了一家公司，旨在收集中国占领区的废钢铁，并雇佣了许多中国人从事收集工作。据称，由于国内钢铁短缺，日本人一直在占领区收集这些金属，为了提高效率，他们成立了一家公司或一个钢铁业社团。
南市的原江南船坞与机器工程局已被改建为日本造船厂，其中大量铁器被没收并移走，连同中国船坞在上海战事期间储存在另一处的铁器一并搬离。
由于这仍无法满足日军的大量需求，去年专门为了在中国收集废钢铁而组织了一家日本钢铁公司。此前，日本人将以此方式获得的废钢铁堆放在杨树浦鱼市场附近的一块空地上，但现在地点已变更。吴淞的文藻浜（音译）已划出一大片区域用于此目的。停泊在吴淞外的日本运输船一直将这些金属运往日本。据说，这就解释了为何在过去几个月里，再也看不到日本运输船在返程途中从杨树浦装载这批贵重货物了。

tained that at 1.30 p.m. 20.12.38, compt. attended 308 Baikal
Road to inspect the scrap iron dump when he saw 4 Japanese come
to the dump riding on M/trucks and immediately commenced to

him that the scrap iron had not been sold to the Japanese and
he had applied for a pass to the J.N.L. Party for removal to
South of Creek. He then came to this station and made this
report.

quantity of scrap iron from various Chinese iron shops prior
to the outbreak of the hostilities and piled same at the said

1938 年 12 月 21 日上午 9 时，一名名叫魏元茂（Wei Yuen Hoh）的中国男子，40 岁，居住于虞洽卿路 567 号，受雇于 D.K.K. 码头办事处，来到本警亭报案称：1938 年 12 月 20 日下午约 1 时 30 分，约 9 吨废铁被日本人从贝加尔路 308 号运走，该处院落内堆放有其拥有的一批废铁。

经 C.D.C. 241 及本报告人调查，查明情况如下：1938 年 12 月 20 日下午 1 时 30 分，报案人前往贝加尔路 308 号检查废铁堆场，当时看见 4 名日本人乘坐摩托卡车来到堆场，并立即开始搬运废铁装车。当时他未加阻止，因为他以为这批废铁已通过一名名叫 Abolnik 的外国经纪人卖给了日本人，他此前曾委托该经纪人处理这批废铁。

1938 年 12 月 2 日上午 8 时，他会见了俄罗斯人 Abolnik，后者告知他废铁并未卖给日本人，且他已向日本海军陆战队（J.N.L. Party）申请通行证，以便将废铁运至苏州河以南地区。随后他便来到本警亭作了此报告。

经讯问，报案人称在战事爆发前，他曾从多家中国铁铺购买大量废铁，并堆放在上述地点。他还表示，他不记得涉事卡车的车牌号码或那些日本人的体貌特征，也与那些日本人素不相识。

Arrest of a Japanese and six Chinese for removing scrap iron from the Kashing Road District under suspicious circumstances.

Sir,

During the past two weeks it has been observed that scrap iron thieves have been very active in the Kashing Road District during the night and early hours of the morning.

Huge quantities of scrap iron and metal have been collected by the thieves and deposited in secluded alleyways at various points in the district evidently in preparation for removal at the first favourable opportunity.

Sir,

With reference to a news item which appeared in the Mainichi on the 7-5-38, which stated that a Japanese subject had been arrested for theft, J.M.P. have made enquiries at the Japanese Consulate and the following has been ascertained:-

On or about 7-5-38 a Japanese named Yuma Tanaka aged 40, residing at No. 304 Nanzing Road, together with an employee named Motoru Deguchi removed by motor trucks a total of 4,000 pairs of aluminium shoe lasts value $14,000.00 from the Chinese owned Tsung Tah (振泰) Rubber Factory situated at Lane 312 No. 31 Dalny Road to the Tanaka Iron Works 304 Nanking Road.

At the time Tanaka carried out the removal the Tsung Tah Factory was being used by Japanese troops as a billet, but he explained to them that he was a personal friend of the factory owner and had been authorised by him to remove the property.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE / m3. / 26 MAY 1938 / SPECIAL BRANCH）

Since the soldiers in occupation were to a certain extent responsible for the factory and contents whilst billeted therein, and in order that the removal should not be later attributed to them, upon leaving they informed the Landing Party Patrol, who in turn passed on the information to the Consulate Police.

Detective Sergeant Higuchi attached to the Consulate Police conducted enquiries & arrested Tanaka and Deguchi and recovered the property. A representative of the Tsung Tah Factory named Yang Shau Tsung (楊孝斯) now residing at No. 36 Rue de la Mission, French Concession has attended the Japanese Consulate and identified the property but he declined to prefer any charge against Tanaka or Deguchi. Both men however are still in custody at the Consulate, & it is understood that a charge of Looting will be preferred against them.

先生，

关于5月7日（1938年）《每日新闻》（Mainichi）刊登的一则新闻，该新闻称一名日本臣民因盗窃被捕，日本警务处（J.M.P.）已向日本领事馆查询，查明情况如下：

1938年5月7日前后，一名名为田中勇马（Yuma Tanaka，音译）、40岁、居住于南京路304号的日本人，与其名为出口元（Motoru Deguchi，音译）的雇员，用卡车将共计4,000双铝制鞋楦（价值14,000.00美元）从位于大连路31号312弄、由华人所有的振泰橡胶厂运至南京路304号的田中铁工厂。

田中进行搬运时，振泰工厂正被日军用作营房，但他向日军解释称他是工厂厂主的私人朋友，并已获得厂主授权搬走这些财产。

（印：上海公共租界工部局警务处 / m3. / 1938年5月26日 / 特别分部）

由于驻守士兵在一定程度上对驻扎期间的工厂及其内部物品负有责任，且为了日后不将此次搬运归咎于他们，士兵在离开时通知了登陆部队巡逻队，后者又将此信息转告给领事馆警察。

隶属于领事馆警察的警探长樋口（Higuchi，音译）进行了调查，逮捕了田中和出口，并追回了财物。现居住于法租界Mission路（今四川南路附近，原文为Rue de la Mission）36号的振泰工厂代表杨孝斯已前往日本领事馆辨认了该批财物，但他拒绝控告田中或出口。然而，两人目前仍被拘留在领事馆，据悉将对他们提出抢劫指控。

追回的财物目前存放于日本——

At 12.55 p.m. 7-4-38 a telephone message was received
from an Indian (British) watchman employed at the Lester
Institute, Yuenfong Road, reporting that Japanese soldiers
were removing furniture from houses located at East Seward
and Yuenfong Road corner.
Enquiries were made and it was learned that at about
12.40 p.m. 7-4-38 a party of about twenty Japanese soldiers
with a Motor Truck appeared outside the entrance of alleyway
No.235 Yuenfong Road, which is the property of Messrs A.K.
Burkill and sons., 20 Canton Road. The soldiers entered the
alleyway and proceeded to enter various houses. The head
watchman, one Telok Singh, employed by the above Company,
accosted one of the men, who appeared to be an Officer, and
asked him what he wanted. The Officer replied in English and
stated that he was going to remove property from the houses.
The watchman pointed out that the property was British and
that he could not permit its removal. The Officer then
produced a piece of paper and stated that he had permission
from the Consulate to remove the property. He did not say
which Consulate. The watchman insisted that the Property
could not be removed whereupon the Officer seized hold of his
arms and bumped him twice against the wall after which he was
taken into one of the houses and a guard of one soldier
placed over him.
The soldiers then proceeded to remove furniture from
the houses and load it onto the truck. This continued for
about 20 minutes after which the Officer called the soldier
who was guarding the watchman away and all the soldiers to-
gether with the truck loaded with furniture drove away south-
wards along Yuenfong Road turning eastwards into Seward Road
and disappeared.
Enquiries proceeding.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL - 8 APR 1938 SPECIAL BRANCH）

French Police
secure the
release of an
Annomite from
the custody of
the Japanese
Military
Gendarmerie.
Misc. 192/38.

At about 12 noon April 2nd 1938 the Master of the French
liner "Jean Laborde", which was then moored alongside the
Hongkew and Shanghai Wharf, discovered the absence from the
ship of an Annamite seaman named Hoang Van Than. The vessel
sailed for Europe on 4-4-38 and at time of sailing the seaman
had not returned.
The French Police were notified through the French
Consulate of the man's disappearance and enquiries were
instituted.
At about 3.10 p.m. 7-4-38, D.S.I. Yankevsky of the French
Police called at Hongkew Station in the course of his enquiries
after the missing man. He was accompanied to the Japanese
Military Gendarmerie Headquarters by a Japanese detective in
an effort to find out if the man was being held there. The
detectives were informed that no such person was in the
custody of the Gendarmerie. The party then returned to
Hongkew Station and reported their failure to find the man.
It was within the knowledge of detectives attached to
this Station that a man answering Hoang's description was in
the custody of the Japanese Military Gendarmerie on the 5-4-38.
This information was conveyed to D.S.I. Yankevsky whereupon
a second visit was paid to the Gendarmerie Headquarters at
which time the missing man was produced and handed over to the
French Police.

经查询得知，1938年4月7日中午12时40分左右，一队约二十名日本士兵带着一辆卡车出现在圆明园路235弄弄堂口外，该房产属于广东路20号的A.K. Burkill父子商行。士兵进入弄堂，并进入各户房屋。上述公司雇佣的总看守人特洛克·辛格（Telok Singh）拦住了一名看似是军官的人，询问其意图。该军官用英语回答，称他要搬走房屋内的财产。看守人指出财产属英国所有，不允许搬走。该军官随即拿出一张纸，称他有领事馆的许可搬走财产。他未说明是哪个领事馆。看守人坚持不能搬走财产，于是该军官抓住他的手臂，将他两次撞向墙壁，随后他被带入一间房屋，并由一名士兵看守。
士兵们接着从房屋内搬运家具并装上卡车。这一过程持续了约20分钟，之后军官叫回看守看守人的士兵，所有士兵连同装满家具的卡车一起沿圆明园路向南驶去，转入西华德路向东消失。
调查正在进行中。

Nippon Marines
Seize Property
Of British Firm

Godown Ordered Open,
Goods Of Heath
Firm Looted

OFFICER STATED
ACTING ON ORDER

British Consul Officials
Notified; Loss Totals
Declared High

Wholesale looting of British property in north of the creek Settlement areas by a Japanese Marine partrol has been reported to the British Consulate-General by Heath (1927) Limited, the property loss running into thousands of pounds Sterling.

The company gave the following account of the incident to the consular authorities in announcing its losses yesterday:
“At 7 o’clock this morning a Japanese Naval Landing Party Patrol drew up and demanded under threat that our warehouse be opened. The Shanghai Municipal Police watchman opened the gates. Several Japanese entered the premises and whilst the watchman was away reporting the incident to the Municipal Police they ransacked the premises, opened the safes and removed a quantity of steel and general merchandise. They departed at 9 o’clock.

Acting On Orders
“Sub-Lieutenant Kushige informed the Shanghai Municipal Police that he was acting under instructions. Heath (1927) Limited is a duly registered British company having the name on a signboard outside the premises which was shown to Kushige who, although told the property inside was British-owned, insisted upon taking away several thousands of pounds worth.
“Sub-Lieutenant Kushige stated that he had taken 150 lengths of steel tubes, but failed to mention all other property which was also taken away.”

Old Question
The question of looting of scrap iron from Japanese-controlled Settlement areas has been raised frequently during the past few weeks, pictures appearing in the local press to show how the Japanese were getting metal for their war industries, but this is the first known case of a Japanese patrol invading foreign property under orders to remove cargo. There have been cases of evacuated houses being entered and the property of foreigners removed by the Japanese, but when questioned about such incidents Nipponese spokesmen stated that the action was taken to “protect” the property and store it in a safer place so as to avoid looting.

What action has been taken by the British authorities could not be ascertained up to press time, important consular officials being engaged in welcoming the new Ambassador to China. It is presumed, however, that a strong protest has been filed with the Japanese authorities and a demand made for the return of the property.

该公司昨日在向领事当局通报损失时，对事件经过作了如下陈述：
“今天早上7点，一支日本海军登陆队巡逻队驶来，并以威胁手段要求打开我们的仓库。工部局警务处的看守打开了大门。几名日本人进入院内，趁看守离开去工部局警务处报告此事之际，他们搜查了院落，打开保险箱，搬走了大量钢材和一般商品。他们于9点离开。

奉命行事
“久志格（Kushige）少尉告知工部局警务处，他是奉命行事。希思（1927）有限公司是一家正式注册的英国公司，其名称标示在院外的招牌上，该招牌已出示给久志格观看。尽管被告知内部财产属英国所有，久志格仍坚持要拿走价值数千英镑的物品。
“久志格少尉称他拿走了150根钢管，但未提及也被拿走的所有其他财产。”

老问题
过去几周内，人们频繁提出从日本控制的租界地区掠夺废铁的问题，当地报刊也刊登图片，显示日本人如何为其战争工业获取金属，但这是已知的第一起日本巡逻队奉命入侵外国财产以移除货物的案件。此前曾发生过日军进入已疏散房屋并移除外国人财产的情况，但当就此类事件进行质询时，日本发言人称，采取此类行动是为了“保护”财产，并将其存放在更安全的地方，以避免被抢劫。

截至发稿时，尚无法确定英国当局采取了何种行动，因为重要的领事官员正忙于欢迎新任驻华大使。然而，据推测，已向日本当局提出强烈抗议，并要求归还财产。

February 8, 1938. Morning Translation.

Ta Mei Wan Pao published the following editorial on Feb. 7 :-

THE DUTIES OF THE POLICE

Although it seems too late now to talk about
the removal of machinery in Hongkew, it may be more useful
to have the case dealt with legally. Chinese property
owners are not in a position to find out what has become of
their property for they cannot enter Hongkew District and
have to depend on reports made by foreign merchants.
We have no desire to increase the work of
the Shanghai Municipal Police, but according to common
reasoning, since Chinese property has been removed by some
persons, the Police should, at least, endeavour to put
a stop to the removal after receiving such reports.
Good result could have been obtained if the Police
authorities had managed to stop this well-organized daylight
robbery. The least the Police could do was to do their
best to protect the property or to conduct an investigation
to ascertain the nature of the organization and the kind
of persons who are removing Chinese property, because
such removal of property might have not been done with the
approval of the Japanese military authorities. It is
a black mark against the senior Japanese military officers
for not making a frank acknowledgment. There is some
doubt in the case because up to the present the Japanese
have not made any such public announcement on the following
lines, for instance, "As we are short of scrap iron and
other materials for the manufacture of firearms, we have
to rob Chinese iron works and remove the scrap iron from
those works to Japan". According to our observation,
the removal of iron may have been promoted by a certain
private organization with which the Japanese authorities
did not care to interfere. All other property in the
Hongkew District will be stolen if such acts of robbery
are allowed to continue. If strong action is adopted,
such acts will be curbed.
The Police should, at least, conduct an
investigation into the amount of machinery and other
articles that have been removed and should do their utmost
to put a stop to such removals. If the Police
cannot do this, they should, at least, publish the facts
regarding such removals.
(Note: This editorial also appears in the "Shanghai
Evening Post & Mercury".)

《大美晚报》于2月7日发表以下社论：-

警察的职责

虽然现在谈论虹口机器搬迁之事似乎为时已晚，但从法律角度处理此案或许更为有益。中国业主无法查明其财产的下落，因为他们无法进入虹口区，只能依赖外商的报告。
我们无意增加上海公共租界工部局警务处的工作负担，但根据常理推断，既然中国人的财产被某些人搬走，警方在接到此类报告后，至少应努力制止搬迁行为。如果警方当局能够制止这种有组织的白天抢劫，本可取得良好效果。警方至少应尽最大努力保护财产，或进行调查以查明组织性质以及搬运中国财产的人员种类，因为此类财产搬运行为可能并未得到日本军方的批准。日本高级军官未作出坦率承认，这是一个污点。此案存在一些疑点，因为截至目前，日本人尚未发布如下内容的公开声明，例如：“由于我们缺乏制造枪械所需的废铁和其他材料，我们必须抢劫中国的铁厂，并将废铁从这些工厂运往日本”。据我们观察，铁的搬运可能是由某个私人组织推动的，日本当局对此不愿干涉。如果允许此类抢劫行为继续下去，虹口区的所有其他财产都将被盗。如果采取强硬行动，此类行为将受到遏制。
警方至少应对已搬走的机器和其他物品的数量进行调查，并竭尽全力制止此类搬运行为。如果警方做不到这一点，他们至少应公布有关此类搬运的事实。
（注：这篇社论也出现在《字林西报》上。）

January 27, 1938. Morning Translation.

Hwa Mei Wen Pao Morning Edition :-

JAPANESE REMOVING SCRAP IRON AND MACHINERY

Nearly all the scrap iron has been removed from Yangtsepoo district by the Japanese, according to information from foreign sources. Ever since the outbreak of the hostilities in Shanghai, the Japanese have been collecting iron in the districts under their occupation. At first they removed the iron stored in Chinese warehouses along North Soochow Road, later they began to concentrate their attention to the removal of machinery in the factories, godowns and dwelling houses that had escaped destruction.

According to information, large quantities of such scrap iron are at present piled up along the wharves on Chemulpo Road and behind the Customs Jetty on Lay Road. It is believed that several hundreds of tons of such iron have already been removed to Japan.

According to certain persons who went to Yangtsepoo to make an inspection several days ago, a number of Chinese coolies were noticed busily removing machinery from the factories, especially from the Nanyang Brothers Tobacco Factory. The coolies worked under the supervision of Japanese.

Sin Wen Pao and other local newspapers :-

CHINESE BANKS AND THE LUNAR NEW YEAR

Although January 30, the day for a general settlement of accounts, is Sunday and is therefore a holiday, the Chinese Bankers' Association and the Native Bankers' Guild, at a joint meeting held recently, decided that all their member banks are to carry on business as usual on that day in order to facilitate the work of settlement of their accounts. Commencing from January 31, the foreign style banks will close for three days, while the native banks will close for four days.

THE RELIEF OF REFUGEES

At the request of the International Relief Commission of the China Red Cross Society, the Shanghai Chinese Chamber of Commerce has notified local trades to collect from their employees 2% of their monthly salaries for the relief of refugees. This is already being done by local banks.

《华美晚报》晨刊：-

日本人搬运废铁和机器

据外籍人士消息，杨树浦区的废铁几乎已被日本人搬空。自上海战事爆发以来，日本人一直在其占领区收集铁器。起初，他们搬走北苏州路沿线中国仓库中储存的铁器，后来开始集中注意力，搬走那些幸免于毁坏的工厂、仓库和住宅中的机器。

据悉，目前大量此类废铁堆积在杰缪尔波路（Chemulpo Road，即今昌化路附近音译，或指具体码头路）的码头沿线以及雷路（Lay Road，即今九江路或延安东路附近音译，此处指海关栈桥后）的海关栈桥后面。据信，已有数百吨此类铁器被运往日本。

据几天前前往杨树浦视察的一些人称，注意到许多中国苦力正忙着从工厂搬运机器，特别是从南洋兄弟烟草厂。苦力们在日本人的监督下工作。

《新闻报》及其他本地报纸：-

中国银行与农历新年

虽然1月30日是统一结账日，恰逢星期日，因此是假日，但上海银行公会和上海钱业公会在最近举行的联席会议上决定，为了便于结账工作，其所有会员银行在该日均照常营业。从1月31日起，外商银行将停业三天，而钱庄将停业四天。

《华美晚报》晨刊：-

难民救济

应中国红十字会国际救济委员会的请求，上海总商会已通知本地商界从其员工月薪中抽取2%用于难民救济。本地银行已在执行此举。
